26. Mr. Yusuf submits that though special time limit is given there, it will not be hit by section 28 of the Contract Act in view of the fact that by agreement the party waived his right and as such the Limitation Act will not be a bar to give effect to the condition of the agreement. In this connection Mr. Yusuf has referred to the cases of Pearl Insurance Company Vs. Atma Ram, AIR 1960 (Punjab), 236 and Volcan Insurance Vs. Maharaj Singh AIR 1976 (SC) 287. In both the aforesaid decisions this question of limitation of this special period mentioned in condition No. 19 of the agreement was referred to and it was held by their Lordships that this special period of limitation will not be hit by section 28 of the Contract Act inasmuch as this limitation was created by consent of the parties and that will amount to waiver of the right given under Limitation Act. Mr. Yusuf further submits that in Condition No. 19 it is stated "subject to pending action or arbitration." He submits that this word "action" is not an ordinary action or other action. But it will amount to a judicial proceeding pending in a court. This action will mean the suit in a civil Court for recovering damage. So, Mr. Yusuf submits that the present case is fully covered under this Condition No. 19 of this fire insurance policy Ext. 3. 

 29. The meaning of the word "action" is given in the Law Dictionary by PS Collin where it is shown that the action means thing which has been done or to take action. It also means Court action in civil case in any law Court; Action for damages; action for libel or libel action, to bring an action for damages against anyone. He has also referred to Webster's Dictionary where the action means that the state of being active as opposed to rest; that effect of one body upon another; the performance of a function effective motion. In Corpus Juris Secundum, Vol. 1 action has been defined in this way that the word is derived from the Latin "ago" to urge and drive. In its general sense, an act or series of acts; behaviour; the condition of acting; conduct.Something done. In its special legal sense, it is referring to judicial proceedings. The word is elsewhere defined and fully treated in the title actions. In Judicial Dictionary, 11th Edition by KJ Alyars wherein the definition of action has been given in this way that the word "action" occurring in Clause 13 of the insurance policy means an action by the party to enforce the terms of the policy. In other words, action in the present context would mean legal demand for enforcement of right of the plaintiff before, filing the suit. "Proceeding" (would) be a word with a larger meaning than" action". Every action is a proceeding, but it is not possible "to say that every proceeding is an action". He has also referred to Macgillivary in Insurance Law Relating to All Risks other Than Marine, 4th Edition, Section 1, page 1798, paragraph 1794 which speaks about conditions relating to limitation of action. A limitation of the period within which action can be brought after loss is valid, notwithstanding that it gives a shorter period than the : Limitation Act, 1939. The limitation sometimes runs from the time when the money becomes payable, as where it is payable so many days after proof of loss, but more usually the limitation runs from the date of loss; if the insurers cause delay in the settlement of the loss, or induce the assured to refrain from commencing proceedings by promise of payment or definite hopes of settlement, the condition may be held to be waived or the period may be held to have been enlarged by suspension of the condition during negotiation for settlement.
